ety.text: From Middle English date, from Old French date, datil, datille, from Latin dactylus (likely via Old Provençal datil), from Ancient Greek δάκτυλος (dáktulos, “finger”) (from the resemblance of the date to a human finger), probably a folk-etymological alteration of a word from a Semitic source such as Arabic دَقَل (daqal, “variety of date palm”) or Hebrew דֶּקֶל (deqel, “date palm”). Doublet of dactyl and dactylus. Displaced native Old English fingeræppel, literally "finger-apple".
From Middle English date, from Old French date, from Late Latin data, from Latin datus (“given”), past participle of dare (“to give”); from Proto-Indo-European *deh₃- (“to give”). Doublet of data.

senses.d: The fruit of the date palm, Phoenix dactylifera, somewhat in the shape of an olive, containing a soft, sweet pulp and enclosing a hard kernel.
ex: We made a nice cake from dates.

senses.d: The date palm.
ex: There were a few dates planted around the house.

senses.d: The anus.
ex: The bullet took the middle finger of his right hand clean off […]. ‘He sure won't be sticking that finger up his date again,’ said Max.
Black Superman could kiss his date, the little faggot.

senses.d: The addition to a writing, inscription, coin, etc., which specifies the time (especially the day, month, and year) when the writing or inscription was given, executed, or made.
ex: the date of a letter, of a will, of a deed, of a coin, etc.
US date : 05/24/08 = Tuesday, May 24th, 2008. UK date : 24/05/08 = Tuesday 24th May 2008.

senses.d: A specific day in time at which a transaction or event takes place, or is appointed to take place; a given point of time.
ex: the date for pleading
The start date for the festival is September 2.

senses.d: A point in time.
ex: You may need that at a later date.

senses.d: An assigned end; a conclusion.
ex: What Time would spare, from Steel receives its date.

senses.d: A given or assigned length of life; duration.
ex: Good luck prolonged hath thy date.

senses.d: A pre-arranged meeting.
ex: I arranged a date with my Australian business partners.

"Why, Mr. Nisbet! I thought you were in New York."
"I had a telegram this morning, calling the date off,"

senses.d: One's companion for social activities or occasions, especially a romantic partner.
ex: I brought Melinda to the wedding as my date.

senses.d: A romantic meeting or outing with a lover or potential lover, or the person so met.
ex: We really hit it off on the first date, so we decided to meet the week after.
The cinema is a popular place to take someone on a date.

senses.d: To note the time or place of writing or executing; to express in an instrument the time of its execution.
ex: to date a letter, a bond, a deed, or a charter
You will be surprised, I don't question, to find among your correspondencies in foreign parts, a letter dated from Blois.

senses.d: To note or fix the time of (an event); to give the date of.
ex: The writer dates the festival on June 21st, which is probably a mistake.

senses.d: To determine the age of something.
ex: to date the building of the pyramids

senses.d: To take (someone) on a date, or a series of dates.
To have a steady relationship with; to be romantically involved with.
ex: Jessica Simpson reportedly went on a drinking binge after discovering ex-boyfriend John Mayer is dating Jennifer Aniston.

senses.d: To have a steady relationship with each other; to be romantically involved with each other.
ex: They met a couple of years ago, but have been dating for about five months.

senses.d: To make or become old, especially in such a way as to fall out of fashion, become less appealing or attractive, etc.
ex: This show hasn't dated well.
The comedian dated himself by making quips about bands from the 1960s.

senses.d: To have beginning; to begin; to be dated or reckoned.
ex: The Batavian republic dates from the successes of the French arms.

senses.d: A representation of information in a computer (as symbols, quantities, sound, images or videos) which is stored, processed or transmitted in the form of electrical signals, records on magnetic tape or punched cards, etc.
